dataset.note: Baseline statuses and dates below are copied verbatim from web-features@3.45.0. This is a snapshot: re-run the generator to refresh it.

features.name: AbortController and AbortSignal
features.description: The AbortController and AbortSignal APIs allow you to cancel an ongoing operation, such as a fetch() request.
features.removable_action: Delete the abortcontroller-polyfill import and its bundler alias; AbortController and AbortSignal are available natively.

features.name: Anchor positioning
features.description: Anchor positioning places an element based on the position of another element. For example, you can place a tooltip next to the content it references.
features.risk_action: Anchor positioning is not Baseline in any browser set yet. Keep a JavaScript positioner, or gate the CSS behind @supports (anchor-name: --a).
features.removable_action: Do not remove the JavaScript positioner yet. This is a forward pointer only: when CSS anchor positioning reaches the level you target, most tether/flip logic collapses into anchor-name, position-anchor and position-try-fallbacks.

features.name: Animations (CSS)
features.description: The animation CSS property animates an element's style over time, using keyframes described in @keyframes rules.
features.removable_action: Drop the -webkit- animation declarations and the @-webkit-keyframes block; the unprefixed forms are enough.

features.name: appearance
features.description: The appearance CSS property controls the appearance of form controls. Using appearance: none disables any default native appearance and allows the elements to be styled with CSS.
features.removable_action: Delete the prefixed declarations and keep appearance: none.

features.name: aspect-ratio
features.description: The aspect-ratio CSS property controls the width-to-height ratio of elements. For and
features.removable_action: The @supports guard around aspect-ratio always passes now. Unwrap the block and delete the padding-top ratio hack it was protecting.

features.name: Async clipboard
features.description: The navigator.clipboard API asynchronously reads and writes to the system clipboard.
features.risk_action: navigator.clipboard.write / read need a fallback at this target. document.execCommand('copy') still works as one, or feature-detect with 'clipboard' in navigator.

features.name: backdrop-filter
features.description: The backdrop-filter CSS property applies graphical effects such as blurring or color shifting to the area behind an element.
features.risk_action: backdrop-filter degrades to no blur rather than breaking, but the panel behind it may become unreadable. Set an opaque fallback background-color first, then override it inside @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)).
features.removable_action: Safari has shipped the unprefixed property since 18, so -webkit-backdrop-filter is only needed for older Safari. Remove it once your target no longer includes those versions.

features.name: border-radius
features.description: The border-radius CSS property rounds the corners of the border drawn around an element.
features.removable_action: Delete the prefixed declarations; border-radius has been unprefixed everywhere for years.

features.name: box-shadow
features.description: The box-shadow CSS property applies shadow effects around an element's frame. This can create drop shadow and inner shadow effects.
features.removable_action: Delete the prefixed declarations; box-shadow has been unprefixed everywhere for years.

features.name: Cascade layers
features.description: The @layer CSS at-rule avoids specificity conflicts by providing priority levels for different groups of CSS rules, such as low-priority styles like resets, and high-priority styles like UI components.
features.risk_action: A browser that does not understand @layer drops the whole block, so the layered rules vanish rather than losing priority. Ship the styles unlayered at this target.

features.name: clip-path
features.description: The clip-path CSS property and SVG attribute set the visible area of an element. Everything outside the area will be hidden.
features.removable_action: Delete -webkit-clip-path and keep the unprefixed declaration.

features.name: color-mix()
features.description: The color-mix() function mixes two colors in a given color space and by a given amount. Commonly, lighter or darker variations of a color are created by mixing with white or black.
features.risk_action: color-mix() in an unsupported browser makes the whole declaration invalid, so the property falls back to its inherited or initial value. Precede it with a static colour declaration.

features.name: Container queries (size)
features.description: Container size queries with the @container (…) at-rule apply styles to an element based on a dimension of its container, such as width or height.
features.risk_action: A dropped @container block leaves the element at its default styling. Write the mobile-first rule outside the container query so the unstyled state is the usable one.
features.removable_action: The @supports guard for container queries always passes now, and container-query-polyfill can leave the bundle.

features.name: content-visibility
features.description: The content-visibility CSS property delays rendering an element, including layout and painting, until it is needed.
features.risk_action: content-visibility: auto is a progressive enhancement, but contain-intrinsic-size must be set with it or scrollbars jump. Unsupported browsers simply render everything.

features.name: Custom properties
features.description: Custom properties are CSS properties prefixed with -- that set values you can reuse with the var() function. For example, you can set a --key-color property to reuse as border-color: var(--key-color). Also known as CSS variables.
features.removable_action: Remove css-vars-ponyfill and its build step; custom properties resolve natively.

features.name: <dialog>
features.description: The <dialog> HTML element represents a modal or non-modal dialog box, such as a confirmation prompt or a subwindow used to enter data.
features.removable_action: Remove dialog-polyfill, its stylesheet and the registerDialog() calls; <dialog>, showModal() and ::backdrop are native.

features.name: Fetch
features.description: The fetch() method makes asynchronous HTTP requests.
features.removable_action: Remove the fetch polyfill import and any bundler alias for it.

features.name: field-sizing
features.description: The field-sizing CSS property allows form controls such as <textarea> to be sized based on their content.
features.risk_action: field-sizing: content is a recent addition. Keep the JavaScript autogrow or the rows/cols sizing you already have as the fallback.

features.name: filter
features.description: The filter CSS property applies one or more graphic effects to an element. You can use filter functions, such as blur() and drop-shadow(), alone or combined to produce different effects. For instance, filter: blur(2px).
features.removable_action: Delete -webkit-filter and keep the unprefixed declaration. This is not the same property as backdrop-filter.

features.name: Flexbox
features.description: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system, which places content either horizontally or vertically, with optional wrapping.
features.removable_action: Delete the -webkit- flexbox declarations and the @supports (display: flex) guard. Note that display: -webkit-box and -webkit-box-orient are deliberately NOT reported: they are still load-bearing for -webkit-line-clamp.

features.name: Flexbox gap
features.description: The gap CSS property in a flexbox layout sets the size of the space between items.
features.removable_action: The @supports (gap: ...) guard always passes now. Unwrap it and delete the negative-margin gutter fallback underneath.

features.name: :focus-visible
features.description: The :focus-visible CSS pseudo-class selects elements that match the :focus pseudo-class and meets the browser's criteria for visually emphasizing focused elements.
features.removable_action: Remove the focus-visible polyfill script, the .js-focus-visible / .focus-visible class plumbing and the @supports selector(:focus-visible) guard. Style :focus-visible directly.

features.name: Grid
features.description: CSS grid is a two-dimensional layout system, which lays content out in rows and columns.
features.removable_action: The @supports (display: grid) guard always passes now. Unwrap the block and delete the float or inline-block fallback it was guarding.

features.name: :has()
features.description: The :has() CSS functional pseudo-class matches an element if any of the selectors passed as parameters would match at least one element.
features.risk_action: :has() fails the whole selector list in a browser that does not support it, so the rule never applies. Keep a class toggled from JavaScript at this target.
features.removable_action: The @supports selector(:has(...)) guard always passes now, and the css-has-pseudo build step can be dropped.

features.name: Hyphenation
features.description: The hyphens CSS property controls when long words are broken by line wrapping. Although called hyphens, the property applies to word-splitting behavior across languages, such as customary spelling changes or the use of other characters. Support for non-English languages varies significantly.
features.removable_action: Delete -webkit-hyphens and -ms-hyphens; the unprefixed property is enough. Keep the lang attribute on the document, which hyphenation still needs.

features.name: Intersection observer
features.description: The IntersectionObserver API asynchronously observes changes in the intersection of a target element with an ancestor element or with a top-level document's viewport.
features.removable_action: Remove the intersection-observer polyfill import; the API is native.

features.name: lh unit
features.description: The lh CSS length unit corresponds to the requested line height, the computed value of the line-height property. Some lines may be higher than this based on their content.
features.risk_action: The lh unit resolves to the element's line box height. Replace it with a calc() over your line-height variable at this target.

features.name: light-dark()
features.description: The light-dark() CSS function accepts two colors and uses one depending on the current color scheme.
features.risk_action: light-dark() makes the whole declaration invalid where it is unsupported. Declare the light value normally and override it inside a prefers-color-scheme media query.

features.name: Masks
features.description: The mask CSS property (and several longhand properties) partially or completely hides an element according to the shape and depth of an image.
features.risk_action: An unsupported mask property leaves the element unmasked and fully visible, which is usually worse than not applying the effect. Gate it behind @supports.
features.removable_action: Delete the -webkit-mask declarations and keep the unprefixed ones.

features.name: object-fit
features.description: The object-fit CSS property sets how images, videos, and other replaced elements are scaled within their container.
features.removable_action: The @supports (object-fit: ...) guard always passes now, and object-fit-images / objectFitPolyfill can be deleted along with the background-image fallbacks they drove.

features.name: Oklab and OkLCh
features.description: The Oklab color space expresses colors in terms of lightness and how red/green and blue/yellow a color is, aiming to match how humans perceive colors. OkLCh is a variant of Oklab with polar coordinates. These color spaces can be used with the CSS oklab() and oklch() functions.
features.risk_action: oklch() and oklab() invalidate the declaration where they are unsupported. Put an sRGB hex or rgb() declaration immediately before as the fallback.

features.name: Popover
features.description: The popover HTML attribute creates an overlay to display content on top of other page content. Popovers can be shown declaratively using HTML, or using the showPopover() method.
features.risk_action: The popover attribute is inert where unsupported: the element stays in the flow and visible. Keep the polyfill or the JavaScript dialog at this target.
features.removable_action: Remove @oddbird/popover-polyfill and its stylesheet; popover, popovertarget and showPopover() are native.

features.name: Resize observer
features.description: The ResizeObserver API observes and reacts to changes in the size of DOM elements.
features.risk_action: Fall back to a window resize listener, or keep a polyfill, at this target.
features.removable_action: Remove resize-observer-polyfill / @juggle/resize-observer and use the global ResizeObserver.

features.name: rlh unit
features.description: The rlh CSS length unit is a font-relative length relative to the line height of root element.
features.risk_action: The rlh unit resolves against the root line box. Replace it with a calc() over a root custom property at this target.

features.name: @scope
features.description: The @scope CSS at-rule sets the scope for a group of rules.
features.risk_action: An unsupported @scope block is dropped entirely, taking its rules with it. Scope with a class or a data attribute at this target.

features.name: scroll-behavior
features.description: The scroll-behavior CSS property controls whether scrolling is smooth or snaps, for scroll actions not performed by the user such as those triggered by navigation.
features.removable_action: Remove smoothscroll-polyfill and its polyfill() call; scroll-behavior: smooth and the behavior: 'smooth' scroll options work natively.

features.name: scrollbar-gutter
features.description: The scrollbar-gutter CSS property reserves space for the scrollbar, preventing unwanted layout changes as the scrollbar appears and disappears.
features.risk_action: Without scrollbar-gutter the layout shifts when a scrollbar appears. That is the pre-existing behaviour, so this is a safe enhancement, but do not rely on the reserved space in measurements.

features.name: Shared worker
features.description: The SharedWorker() constructor runs a script in its own thread, which can send and receive messages with other scripts running at the same origin.
features.risk_action: SharedWorker is missing on some targets and has historically been absent from Chrome on Android. Feature-detect and fall back to a dedicated Worker per tab, or to BroadcastChannel for cross-tab messaging.

features.name: @starting-style
features.description: The @starting-style CSS at-rule sets the starting values for properties that are transitioning when the target element's style is first updated.
features.risk_action: Without @starting-style the entry transition simply does not play; the end state still applies. Safe as an enhancement, but do not put required styles inside the block.

features.name: Sticky positioning
features.description: The position: sticky CSS declaration positions an element in the normal flow until it crosses a specified threshold, at which points it becomes fixed (stuck) at that position.
features.removable_action: Delete position: -webkit-sticky and the @supports (position: sticky) guard.

features.name: structuredClone()
features.description: The structuredClone() global method creates a deep copy of an object. Values that cannot be cloned can instead be transferred, making the original value no longer usable.
features.risk_action: Fall back to a manual deep clone at this target; JSON round-tripping is not equivalent for Map, Set, Date or typed arrays.
features.removable_action: Remove @ungap/structured-clone and call the global structuredClone().

features.name: Subgrid
features.description: The subgrid value for the grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties allows a grid item to inherit the grid definition of its parent grid container.
features.risk_action: grid-template-columns: subgrid is invalid where unsupported and the track list falls back to none, collapsing the nested grid. Declare an explicit track list first.

features.name: text-wrap: balance
features.description: The text-wrap: balance CSS declaration balances the length of each line when text is broken into multiple lines. Also known as headline balancing.
features.risk_action: text-wrap: balance is a typographic nicety; where it is unsupported the text wraps normally. Safe as an enhancement.

features.name: text-wrap: pretty
features.description: The text-wrap: pretty CSS declaration prioritizes better layout over speed when text is broken into multiple lines.
features.risk_action: text-wrap: pretty is not Baseline in any browser set yet. Where it is unsupported the text wraps normally, so it is safe as an enhancement but cannot be relied on.

features.name: 2D transforms
features.description: The transform CSS property and its 2D transform functions allow rotating, scaling, skewing, and translating an element. Arbitrary 2D transforms are also possible using a transformation matrix.
features.removable_action: Delete the prefixed transform declarations and keep the unprefixed ones.

features.name: Transitions (CSS)
features.description: The transition shorthand CSS property sets how changes to an element's styles may occur over time. Transitions can be applied to specific CSS properties, all properties, or none.
features.removable_action: Delete the prefixed transition declarations and keep the unprefixed ones.

features.name: Trusted types
features.description: Trusted types allow you to lock down insecure parts of the DOM API and prevent client-side cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
features.risk_action: Trusted Types enforcement is ignored where unsupported, so the Content-Security-Policy header is defence in depth rather than a guarantee. Keep sanitising on the server, and guard window.trustedTypes before calling createPolicy.

features.name: URLPattern
features.description: The URLPattern API creates patterns that can be matched against URLs or URL components.
features.risk_action: Keep the router's own matcher, or the urlpattern-polyfill, at this target.
features.removable_action: Remove urlpattern-polyfill and use the global URLPattern.

features.name: user-select
features.description: The user-select CSS property controls which elements can be selected by the user.
features.risk_action: user-select is not Baseline: the unprefixed property alone is not enough. Keep -webkit-user-select alongside it. baselinefit therefore never reports that prefix as removable.

features.name: View transitions
features.description: View transitions allow you to create animated visual transitions between different states of a document.
features.risk_action: Guard startViewTransition with a feature test and apply the DOM change directly when it is missing; view-transition-name on its own is inert.

features.name: Small, large, and dynamic viewport units
features.description: The sv*, lv*, and dv* CSS viewport units are relative to the smallest, largest, and current (dynamic) viewport size. They are used to size elements in relation to the viewport's dimensions.
features.risk_action: Precede the dynamic viewport unit with a vh or vw declaration so unsupported browsers keep a usable height.
